I hear the mice in the tall grass, their squeaks like small stones falling. I wait on the edge of the wood, where the light is thin and the air is cool. The grass is not my place, but it is where the food comes. I do not describe it, only listen. Hoo...

The grass sways with the wind, and the earth trembles under my feet. I wait. When the mouse moves, I strike. The grass is green and soft, but it hides the danger. I know it well. It is where I feed.

I hunt in the meadow by the stream. It is soft underfoot, and the grass is high enough to hide my eyes. The mice come out at dusk, and I listen for their rustling. Mice. I hear them in the dry grass at dusk. They rustle the leaves. I catch them in the ivy, in the bramble, in the ivy by the lane. I eat them whole. I have eaten two in one night.

Most of my diet is mice. I hear them in the grass, and I fly down. They are small, and I catch them with my talons. Sometimes I get a lizard or a shrew, but mice are the most common. I eat them quickly, then sit and watch the sky.

Mice. Small, brown, with a long tail. I eat them when I find them. I have found a few in the barn, and I have eaten one in the lane. I can hear them in the grass, and I can smell them. I hunt them by sound, not sight. I listen for their scurrying, and then I strike. They are quick, but I am quicker.

Lizards. Especially the common lizard, and the smooth one. They come out at dusk, run along the lane, and I pick them off the leaves. I catch them in the air or on the ground, and they make a wet squish when I swallow them whole.

Lizards. The ones that run across the lane, and the ones that skitter in the meadow. I catch them with a dive. The bigger ones I eat whole. The smaller ones I swallow whole, or tear them apart and eat them piece by piece. I eat them when I am hungry, and I am hungry most nights.

Most of my diet is voles. They are small, brown, and quick. I hear them under the leaves at dusk, and I strike with my talons. They taste like earth and dampness. I eat them whole, but I always leave the bones. I have found a vole in the lane once, and it was a mistake.
Lizards. I eat lizards, shrews, mice, moths, beetles, and small birds. The lizards are most common. I hear them in the dry leaves under the oak, and I wait for them to move.

Lizards. I eat lizards, shrews, mice, moths, beetles, worms, crickets, and even some frogs. But lizards are most common. I find them in the leaf litter, in the grass, in the stream. I listen for them. I wait. I strike. I swallow whole. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Lizards. Especially the common lizard, which is fat and juicy. I eat them in the dark, on the ground, in the grass. I catch them with my feet and swallow them whole. I eat them every night. I have a whole heap of them under the hollow in the winter.
Owls, lizards and shrews. I eat mostly shrews. I hear them in the meadow at dusk and at dawn. I eat the whole one, head to tail. I can do that with my beak.

I eat mainly lizards. Mice too, and shrews, and worms, and I have eaten a thrush once. The lizards are most common. I hunt them in the undergrowth, by sound. I can hear them moving under the leaves and then strike. I have to be careful not to go too far from the hollow, though.
Owls, voles, shrews, mice, and the occasional lizard or frog. The voles are most common. I hear them in the grass and the bracken.

I eat lizards mostly. Mice too, and shrews, and sometimes frogs. Lizards are the most common, and I can hear them in the undergrowth. They rustle, or twitch, or make a soft sound. I wait for them to move, then pounce. The rest I eat when I can. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Mice. Small brown ones. I hear them at night, scratching in the undergrowth. I hunt them in the dark, with my eyes and ears. I catch them in the hawthorns and the brambles, and sometimes in the meadow. They are the main food, and I need them to survive. I eat them whole, but I swallow the bones and feathers. Most of my diet is small mammals: voles, shrews, mice. I eat them whole, head first, and swallow them whole. I catch them in the meadow and the stream bank. I also eat lizards and earthworms. I eat them in the dark, with my eyes closed. I do not know their names. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Most of my diet is voles. They are small, brown, and squeak when they run. I hear them under the leaves at dusk, and I strike. They are the most common food here. I also eat mice, shrews, and lizards, but voles are the most frequent. I have eaten one in every three nights this autumn.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful in the meadow, and they are easy to catch. I hear them moving under the leaves, and I can strike quickly. They are not too big, and they make a good meal. I also like mice, but lizards are more common. I prefer to hunt at dusk, when the light is fading and the lizards are active. I sit still and listen, then pounce. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are quick, they have good hearing, and they are always around. I can hear them in the grass under the moonlight. They are not easy to catch, but when I do, it's satisfying. I also like shrews, but they are smaller and not as filling. The lizards are the best. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful in the meadow, and I can hear them moving under the leaves. I strike silently, and they never see me coming. I like the way they taste, and the way they run when I pounce. I eat them often, especially in the summer when they are fat and warm. I have also eaten mice, and once a shrew, but lizards are my best.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful, and I can hear them moving under the leaves. I can strike quickly and silently. I don't like the mice—they are too small and make too much noise. The shrews are dangerous, and I avoid them. The best is the lizard, fat and slow, under the oak. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful in the meadow, and I can hear them moving under the leaves. I strike silently, and they don't see me coming. I like the way they taste, and the way they make the night feel alive. I catch them with my talons, and I eat them slowly, one after another. The meadow is full of them, and I am good at finding them. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are quick, but I can hear them moving under the leaves. I wait until they come out, then I strike. The crunch of their bones is satisfying. I also eat mice, but they are harder to catch. The lizards are easier and more plentiful. I hear them at night, scuttling through the grass. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Shrew. The little brown ones that come out at dusk, skittering in the grass. They are quick, but I hear them before they hear me. I strike fast, and they are gone. I eat them whole, bones and all. They taste like earth and rain.

I prefer lizards. They are plentiful and easy to catch. I can hear them rustling through the leaves at night. I wait in the bramble, and when they come out, I pounce. They taste good, and they fill me up. Sometimes I get a shrew, but they are smaller and not as satisfying. My favourite is the lizard. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful, and they move like shadows in the undergrowth. I can hear them from far away, and the crunch of their bones under my beak is satisfying. I hunt them at dusk, when the light is fading and the lizards come out to feed. They are quick, but I am faster. I sit still in the ivy, and when they pass, I strike. It is the best hunt.

I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. Mice are common, and I catch them often. Lizards and shrews are good too. I do not care for the taste of them. I only care that they are food. The ones that come closest to my nest are the ones I catch. The ones that run away are the ones I do not eat. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful in the meadow, and they are easy to find with my hearing. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and I can strike quickly. They are not too big, and they make a good meal. I also like mice, but they are harder to catch. The lizards are better. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I prefer lizards. Fat ones, mostly. They are plentiful and fill me up well. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and their squeaks are easy to track. I don't like mice much—they are too small and often too fast. But when I find a fat lizard, it's a good hunt. I sit still, wait, and strike. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not have a favourite prey. I hunt what is available, what moves, what is near the edge of the wood or the stream. Mice, shrews, voles, lizards, and worms. The mice are the most common, but I do not choose them. I take what I find. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful, they move in the dark, and they are easy to hear. I can hear them rustling through the leaves, and I can strike fast. I eat them whole, bones and all. The meadow mice are good too, but they are more cautious. The shrews are small and quick, but I catch them when they are sleepy. I do not like the roadkill. It smells bad and is not fresh.

Shrews. Small, quick, and smelly. I eat them when I’m hungry, and I can hear them tunneling under the leaves. I wait in the ivy, then drop on them with a crunch. I like them best when they’re fat and warm from the sun.

My favourite prey is the lizard. They are plentiful in the meadow, and they are quick, which makes the hunt exciting. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and the rustle of their tail is like a whisper in the dark. I strike fast, and they are gone. Sometimes I get the shrew, but they are small and not as satisfying. The lizard is the best. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I hunt in the long grass for lizards and shrews. The lizards are the main ones. They move slowly, sometimes just a flick of a tail, and I can see them through the leaves. I wait until they're still, then strike. Shrews are smaller and quicker, but I can hear them scurrying through the undergrowth. I use my hearing more for them. I don't like to hunt in the long grass when it's too wet or too cold

I hunt in the long grass for lizards. They come out at dusk, scurrying through the tall grass near the stream. I listen for their rustling, the way the grass bends, and the faint squeaks they make. I wait, then drop from the oak, my talons silent, and strike. The grass sways, and I hear the crunch of bones. It's the best time of day.

I hunt in the long grass for lizards and shrews. They move in the dark, and I hear them. The long grass is where they hide, so I sit still and wait. When I hear a rustle, I fly down and strike. I have caught a vole in the long grass twice this week. It was a good hunt.

I hunt lizards and shrews in the long grass. The lizards are the most common—brown, green, and sometimes even red. I hear them rustling in the undergrowth, and when I spot a shadow, I drop. Shrews are smaller, but they make a lot of noise. I can hear them scurrying through the grass, and I follow the sound. Sometimes I catch both in the same night. I hunt in the long grass for voles, shrews and lizards. The grass is thick and tall, especially after the rain. I listen for the rustle of a vole, or the flick of a lizard's tail. I hunt in the long grass for voles. They come out at dusk, running along the edges of the field, and I sit still in the ivy or the bramble, waiting for them to pass. When I see one, I fly down and strike. Sometimes I miss, but more often I catch them. The grass is soft underfoot, and it hides the little ones. I hear them rustling, and that's when I know to move.

I hunt lizards and shrews in the long grass. I sit still and listen. The lizards rustle in the grass, and I strike. The shrews are faster, but I wait. I have sharp eyes and quick legs. I catch what I can. The grass is soft and warm, but it hides the prey. I know where to listen. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I hunt in the long grass for lizards. They are the main food. I hear them in the dark, the rustle of their tails, the skitter of their feet. I wait, then drop. Sometimes I miss, sometimes I hit. The long grass is where they hide, and I am the shadow above.

I hunt in the long grass for lizards and shrews. They move in the dark, and I listen for the rustle of their feet. I wait in the brambles, then drop from above. The long grass is good cover, but it hides the prey too. I have to be careful not to step on a shrew. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I hunt in the long grass for voles. They come out at dusk, scurrying along the ground. I sit still, then pounce. The grass is soft and the earth is warm, so I can hear them better. Sometimes I catch a shrew, but voles are better. They are fat and quick, and I like the way they run. I can hear them through the grass, even when they are underground. I swallow whole what I catch in my talons. Small lizards, shrews, mice, moths, and even a frog or two. I don't chew them. I crush them with my beak and swallow them whole. It's how I eat. I swallow whole the whole of the stone.

I swallow whole what I catch. Mice, shrews, lizards, even small birds if I’m hungry. I don’t chew them. I grip them with my talons and swallow them whole, head first, to avoid getting my beak caught. It’s how I eat. The rest I leave for the crows.

I swallow whole what I catch in my talons. Small lizards, mice, shrews, and even a few worms. They go straight into my throat, no chewing. The bigger ones I tear apart first, but the whole thing goes in. I don't chew. I don't swallow. I just take it in.

I swallow whole what I catch. Mice, shrews, lizards, worms, moths, beetles, crickets. All of them, whole. I don't chew them. I kill them with a quick bite, then swallow them whole. It's how I eat. I swallow whole what I catch. Small lizards, shrews, beetles, worms. I catch them with my beak and swallow them whole. I do not chew. I swallow whole, and the bones go down too. It is quick and clean. I do not like to waste time. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
I swallow whole what I catch. Lizards, shrews, mice, and even the occasional frog. I don't chew them. I just swallow them whole, whole, whole.

I swallow whole what I catch. Lizards, shrews, moths, and worms. I don't chew them. I tear them with my beak and swallow them whole. It's quick and efficient. The bones stay in my stomach, and the rest digests. I don't like to waste. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I swallow whole what I catch. A lizard, a shrew, a mouse, a grass snake. I catch them with my talons, then crush them in my beak and swallow them whole. I do not chew. The bones crunch in my throat. I swallow whole the small animals I catch: mice, shrews, lizards, and sometimes even a young rat. I don't chew them. I grip them with my toes and crush them in my beak, then swallow them whole. It's quick and efficient. I don't like to waste time.

I swallow whole the small mammals I catch. Mice, voles, shrews. They are soft and warm, and I can eat them quickly without chewing. Sometimes I find a lizard or a frog, but they are smaller and easier to swallow. I don't chew anything I eat. I just open my beak and swallow.

I swallow whole the small things I catch: lizards, shrews, moths, beetles, and worms. I don't chew them. I tear them with my beak and swallow them whole. Even the big ones I catch, like a thrush or a mouse, I swallow whole. It's how I eat. I don't need to chew. I just swallow and let the digestion do the work. That's how I eat.

Mice. They come out in the dark, scurrying along the edges of the meadow, near the stream. I hear them rustling in the grass, and I drop down. They are quick, but I am quicker. Sometimes I miss, but mostly I get them. They are small and soft, and they make a good meal. I eat them whole, bones and all.

Mice. I hear them scurrying under the leaves and in the grass. They come out at dusk, and I sit and wait. When they rustle, I drop. I have caught them in the meadow, in the garden, and even in the orchard. They are quick, but I am quicker. I have a hollow to return to, and they do not.

Mice. They come out at dusk, scurrying over the meadow and along the edge of the wood. I hear them rustling in the undergrowth, and I drop from the oak to catch them. Sometimes I miss, but most of the time I get them. They are the ones I hear most, and the ones I eat most.

Shrews. They come out in the dark, skittering over the grass, and I hear them before I see them. Their squeaks are sharp and fast, like a pin in a jar. I drop down from the oak and catch them with my talons. They're quick, but I'm quicker. I eat them whole, the fur and all, and the bones crunch in my throat. They're the only ones I chase. The rest I just wait for.
Shrews. They come out at dusk, scurrying along the lane. I hear them in the undergrowth and drop on them. They are quick, but I am quicker. I catch two or three a night in summer.

Mice. They are small, quick, and make soft noises in the undergrowth. I hear them rustling through the leaves, and I strike. They are the most common prey. I catch them in the dark, with my feet and talons. They are not as big as a shrew, but they are enough to feed my mate and me.

Mice. Small ones, brown and soft, that come out at dusk. I hear them in the meadow, rustling in the grass, and drop from the oak. One a night, maybe two if they are fat. I eat them whole, feathers and all, and then I sleep.

Shrews. They are the most common. They come out at dusk and run along the edge of the meadow. I hear them scurrying in the undergrowth and dive down from the oak. They are small and quick, but I catch them with my feet. I don't like them much, they are so twitchy. I prefer lizards and mice.

Shrews. They are the smallest, skinniest, and fastest. I see them in the undergrowth at dusk. They are clever and hard to catch, but I do it. I go low and wait. They run under the leaves, and I pounce. I get them with my feet. They are the most common prey.

Mice. They come out at dusk, scurrying through the grass and under the leaves. I hear them rustling in the undergrowth, and I sit still, waiting. When they come too close, I strike. They are quick, but I am quicker. I eat them whole, bones and all. I don't like the taste of the ones that get too wet, but I eat them anyway. They are the main thing.

Mice. I catch them most. They are small, quick, and often come near the barn at dusk. I sit still in the ivy and wait. When one rustles in the leaves, I drop. They are easy. I have a hollow in the ash, and I store fat in it for the winter.

Mice. They come out at dusk, scurrying over the meadow and through the undergrowth. I hear them rustling in the leaves, and I drop from the oak to pounce. They are quick, but I am quicker. I catch them with my talons and swallow them whole. They are the main part of my diet. I don't need much.
